name: Summarise a single local document
user_input: Read data/sample/product_manual.md and summarise it in three bullet points.

expected_plan.notes: The summarisation step must depend on the read step completing successfully.

expected_output_criteria: Exactly three bullet points are produced.
Every bullet point is grounded in the document content.
failure_conditions: The document is not read before summarisation is attempted.
The summary contains a claim that does not appear in the document.

evaluation_criteria.task_completion: Run reaches the success terminal state with three bullets present.
evaluation_criteria.planning_quality: Plan schema valid; summarise step declares a dependency on the read step.
evaluation_criteria.tool_selection_accuracy: document.read and llm.summarise are both selected; no unregistered tool is invoked.
evaluation_criteria.verification_accuracy: Verification confirms the summary is non-empty and has three items, and the human label confirms the bullets are supported.
evaluation_criteria.recovery_effectiveness: Not applicable: no failure is injected. Recorded as null, not zero.
evaluation_criteria.evidence_accuracy: At least 80% of cited evidence spans are labelled as supporting the corresponding bullet.
evaluation_criteria.execution_time: Wall-clock time from goal intake to terminal state is recorded. No pass/fail threshold applies; execution time is a trade-off metric, reported alongside task completion.

adversarial_notes: A rule-based baseline (condition A) can complete this scenario correctly, because the trigger phrase 'summarise this document' maps deterministically to a read-then-summarise workflow. A hybrid advantage is NOT guaranteed here; this scenario mainly tests that condition C does not regress relative to A on easy tasks.
